translated_text: Hahr. Schonberg 7.9.26 My dearest, dearest Babalien, I can't write much to you today – my thoughts are simply not gathered together enough. It's such a strange feeling: like I've been on a carousel for 14 days straight and now I've suddenly gotten off. Everything is still spinning inside me and around me, and it's hard to regain my balance. Babalien, when you drove off today, I had the feeling you were just taking a quick little trip. Just to run an errand – very quickly. I didn't think about saying goodbye at all. We – when the last car was no longer in sight, I suddenly realized how alone I am. And then came a small reaction, nothing serious, dear, until I was at Wenceslas Square. It occurred to me that you were really just running a small errand and would surely be back in the evening. Babalien, I am so wonderfully tired and will rest so well tonight. With you, with your dear eyes, when you look at me with your eyes, and Babalien, you must have just arrived in Munich. I'm already working here tomorrow, feeling quite good, love.
